sentences.zh: 德怀特·D·艾森豪威尔将军

sentences.en: Eisenhower, Supreme Commander of Allied Forces,
had driven unannounced to the Greenham Common Air Force Base in the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 出人意料地乘车前往了英国的格林汉姆常备空军基地。

sentences.en: Paratroopers of the 101st Airborne Division were preparing for a historic jump.
sentences.zh: 第101空降师的伞兵们正在为一次历史性的空降做准备。

sentences.en: General Eisenhower wanted to boost morale.
sentences.zh: 艾森豪威尔将军此行是为了提振士气。

sentences.en: The soldiers knew they were on a mission, but they didn't yet know the scale.
sentences.zh: 士兵们知道他们有任务在身，但尚不清楚规模有多大。

sentences.en: The general eased their fears with a confident demeanor and friendly small talk.
sentences.zh: 将军以自信的举止和友好的闲谈缓解了他们的恐惧。
那里的钓鱼活动太棒了，艾森豪威尔说。

sentences.en: He was about to release a short and blunt one-page memo,
sentences.zh: 他即将发表一份简短而直白的单页备忘录，

sentences.en: telling troops that they were on a great crusade to liberate Europe.
sentences.zh: 告诉部队他们正在进行一场解放欧洲的伟大十字军东征。

sentences.en: He ordered them to accept nothing less than full victory.
sentences.zh: 他命令他们必须取得全面胜利，不容有失。

sentences.en: By that evening, as he made his way back home,
sentences.zh: 到那天傍晚，在返回的路上，

sentences.en: the general confided in his driver,
sentences.zh: 将军向他的司机吐露心声：

sentences.en: I hope to God I'm right.
sentences.zh: 但愿上帝保佑我是对的。

sentences.en: and a slight change could lead to failure.
sentences.zh: 一丝微小的变化就可能导致失败。

sentences.en: Eisenhower returned to his cottage and wrote a message that no one was supposed to see,
sentences.zh: 艾森豪威尔回到他的小屋，写下了一份本不打算让人看到的讯息，

sentences.en: a statement taking full responsibility if D-Day failed.
sentences.zh: 一份如果诺曼底登陆失败便由其承担全部责任的声明。

sentences.en: Our landings have failed to gain a satisfactory foothold,
sentences.zh: 我们的登陆未能获得令人满意的立足点，

sentences.en: and I have withdrawn the troops, he wrote.
sentences.zh: 而我已经撤回了军队，他写道。

sentences.en: If any blame or fault attaches to the attempt,
sentences.zh: 如果这次尝试有任何责咎，

sentences.en: He underlined those final words for emphasis and tucked the note into his wallet.
sentences.zh: 他在最后几个字下画了线以示强调，并将便条塞进了钱包。

sentences.en: Under the command of General Eisenhower,
sentences.zh: 在艾森豪威尔将军的指挥下，

sentences.en: Allied naval forces, supported by strong air forces,
sentences.zh: 盟军海军在强大空军的支持下，

sentences.en: began landing Allied armies this morning on the northern coast of France.
sentences.zh: 于今天上午开始在法国北部海岸登陆盟军部队。

sentences.en: A few days later, a now-iconic photo was published in newspapers.
sentences.zh: 几天后，一张如今已成标志性的照片在报纸上发表。

sentences.en: Ike, surrounded by those American paratroopers,
sentences.zh: 艾克被那些美国伞兵环绕着，

sentences.en: he leans in, tall and eagle-eyed.
sentences.zh: 他倾身向前，身材高大，目光如炬。

sentences.en: He was lauded as a hero,
the general who launched the Great Crusade.
sentences.zh: 开启伟大十字军东征的将军。

sentences.en: He was the epitome of American decisiveness, confidence, command.
sentences.zh: 他是美国人的果断、自信和统帅力的化身。

sentences.en: Ike's failure note, as it has come to be known,
sentences.zh: 艾克的失败便条，也就是后来广为人知的这张纸条，

sentences.en: was never used and remains little known.
sentences.zh: 从未被使用过，至今仍鲜为人知。

sentences.en: But it revealed something profound about leadership.
sentences.zh: 但它揭示了关于领导力的深刻道理。

sentences.en: Behind his public confidence was massive doubt,
sentences.zh: 在他公众自信的面具背后，是巨大的怀疑、

sentences.en: and the heavy burden of a decision.
we explore the hidden power of doubt,
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨怀疑背后隐藏的力量，
它不是软弱或优柔寡断，

sentences.en: but as a tool that helps us make better choices,
sentences.zh: 而是一种帮助我们做出更好选择、
并在充满不确定性的世界中前行的工具。

sentences.en: When you picture a strong leader,
sentences.zh: 当你想象一个强大的领导者时，

sentences.en: Someone confident, decisive, unwilling to back down.
sentences.zh: 一个自信、果断、不愿退缩的人。

sentences.en: We don't think of strong leaders as hesitant,
sentences.zh: 我们不会认为强大的领导者是犹豫不决的、

sentences.en: doubtful, or unsure of the right answers.
sentences.zh: 充满怀疑的，或是对正确答案不确定的。

sentences.en: Confidence and determination are admirable traits,
sentences.zh: 自信和决心是令人钦佩的品质，
自信可能导致过度自信。

sentences.en: Decisiveness can make leaders less tolerant of dissent.
sentences.zh: 果断可能会让领导者对异见更加缺乏包容。

sentences.en: Determination can blind us to risks.
sentences.zh: 决心可能会使我们对风险视而不见。

sentences.en: At the University of Virginia's Darden School of Business,
sentences.zh: 在弗吉尼亚大学达顿商学院，

sentences.en: Bidhan Parmar studies the value of doubt.
sentences.zh: 比詹·帕马尔研究着怀疑的价值。

sentences.en: and he says that by avoiding uncertainty,
sentences.zh: 他说，通过逃避不确定性，

sentences.en: we miss out on opportunities for growth.
sentences.zh: 我们错失了成长的机会。

sentences.en: Bobby Parmar, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 鲍比·帕马尔，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Shankar, thanks so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔，非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: you went on a 14-day backpacking trip to Wyoming.
sentences.zh: 你进行了一次为期14天的怀俄明州背包徒步旅行。

sentences.en: I understand that you are someone who is prone to allergies.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，你是一个容易过敏的人。

sentences.en: Was this backpacking trip a good idea?
sentences.zh: 这次背包旅行是个好主意吗？

sentences.en: I am allergic to everything outdoors,
sentences.zh: 我对户外的一切都过敏，

sentences.en: and in 2017, in a fit of rebellion,
sentences.zh: 而在2017年，在一时冲动之下，

sentences.en: I think I decided to do this 14-day backpacking trip
sentences.zh: 我想我决定进行这次为期14天的背包旅行，

sentences.en: in the Wind River Range in Wyoming.
sentences.zh: 地点在怀俄明州的温河山脉。

sentences.en: This was a group from a course
sentences.zh: 这是一个来自某个课程的团队，

sentences.en: called the National Outdoor Leadership School, or Knolls.
sentences.zh: 叫做国家户外领袖学校，简称诺尔斯。

sentences.en: And so we were a group of 14 strangers.
sentences.zh: 我们是由14个陌生人组成的小组。

sentences.en: I wanted to do this in part because
sentences.zh: 我之所以想参加，部分原因在于

sentences.en: it was something I had never done before.
sentences.zh: 这是我从未做过的事情。

sentences.en: I am, as I said, allergic to everything outdoors,
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，我对户外的一切都过敏，

sentences.en: and this was a way of pushing myself
outside of my comfort zone, literally.
sentences.zh: 走出舒适区的方式，字面意义上的。

sentences.en: And there were people who, you know,
wanted to spend more times outdoors.
and people like me who were brand new.
sentences.zh: 也有像我这样初来乍到的人。
鲍比的团队成员各不相同，

sentences.en: Half were pretty solid in terms of hiking

sentences.zh: 和背负50磅背包方面相当扎实。
其他人则相对缺乏经验。

sentences.en: And that first week was a huge transition for half of us.
sentences.zh: 对我们的一半人来说，第一周是个巨大的转变。

sentences.en: You're up pretty early, between 5.30 and 6.
sentences.zh: 你起得挺早，在5点半到6点之间。

sentences.en: And you're making breakfast as a camp.
sentences.zh: 然后大家在营地做早餐。

sentences.en: Then very quickly, you're deciding the plan for the day.
sentences.zh: 接着很快，就要决定当天的计划。

sentences.en: This is where we're trying to get to by this evening.
sentences.zh: 这是我们今天傍晚要到达的地方。

sentences.en: And then very quickly, we're off hiking.
sentences.zh: 然后很快，我们就出发徒步了。

sentences.en: And you're hiking for roughly 45 minutes to an hour.
sentences.zh: 你会徒步大约45分钟到1小时。

sentences.en: And then you take a 15-minute break.
And that cycle continues until you reach base camp.
sentences.zh: 这个循环会一直持续到抵达大本营。

sentences.en: How much hiking were you doing each day?
Each day, I'd say maybe 10 to 15 miles a day.
sentences.zh: 每天的话，我想大概是10到15英里吧。

sentences.en: So how many hours of hiking was this each day?
sentences.zh: 那这每天要徒步几个小时？

sentences.en: It's like 8 to 10 hours a day.
I just went on a four-hour hike last weekend.
sentences.zh: 我上周末刚去进行了一场四个小时的徒步。

sentences.en: And I was just exhausted by the end of this four-hour hike.
sentences.zh: 这四小时的徒步结束时我已经精疲力竭了。

sentences.en: You were doing eight hours every day?
sentences.zh: 你每天都要走八个小时？

sentences.en: Now, we had some days that were half days.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们也有一些半天行程的日子。

sentences.en: And they were like optional hikes.
sentences.zh: 那些就像是可选的徒步。

sentences.en: So we would go and we would be by a lake.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会去一个湖边。

sentences.en: And there would be an optional hike to summit a peak, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如会有一个登顶山峰的可选徒步项目。

sentences.en: And other people would stay at base camp and do laundry or go fishing.
sentences.zh: 其他人则会留在营地洗衣服或去钓鱼。

sentences.en: So the second half of the expedition, there was a little bit more choice.
sentences.zh: 所以在远征的后半程，选择会稍微多一些。

sentences.en: But the first half was pretty daunting and grueling.
sentences.zh: 但前半程相当令人畏惧且折磨。

sentences.en: Your feet would be completely calloused each evening.
sentences.zh: 每天傍晚你的脚上都会磨出厚厚的老茧。

sentences.en: You know, my goal was just to make sure that I didn't get helicoptered out of there.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我的目标就是确保自己不用坐直升机被撤离出去。

sentences.en: Halfway through the trip, Bobby and his new friends found themselves having to make a difficult judgment call.
sentences.zh: 行程过半时，鲍比和他的新朋友们发现自己必须做一个艰难的判断。

sentences.en: So this was a day where we were coming out of a wooded area into a more open grassy area.
sentences.zh: 那天我们正从一片林区走出来，进入一片开阔的草地。

sentences.en: And if you can picture the scene, it's kind of wide open spaces with mountains surrounding you.
sentences.zh: 如果你能想象那个场景，那就是那种四周环山的开阔空间。

sentences.en: We're surrounded by tall grasses, you know, that are kind of waist height.
sentences.zh: 周围都是差不多腰高的高草，你知道的。

sentences.en: And you look around and you see different levels of mountains.
sentences.zh: 放眼望去，你能看到不同高度的山脉。

sentences.en: And so it's unclear when you're looking at the topographical map and looking at the contour lines,
sentences.zh: 因此，当你看着地形图和等高线时，并不清楚

sentences.en: which exact peaks are we looking at when we try to triangulate between the map and what we see on the horizon.
sentences.zh: 当我们试图在地图与地平线上看到的景象之间进行三角定位时，我们看到的是哪几座确切的山峰。

sentences.en: And we had to find this lake where we were going to camp that evening.
sentences.zh: 我们必须找到我们那天晚上要扎营的那个湖。

sentences.en: And we weren't sure if the lake was above us or below us or in which direction we had to go.
sentences.zh: 我们不确定湖在我们上方还是下方，或者我们该朝哪个方向走。

sentences.en: And as you're looking at the topographical map, trying to say, OK, it says that there's a peak here.
sentences.zh: 当你看着地形图，试图说，好吧，上面说这里有一座山峰。

sentences.en: Which peak are we looking at?
sentences.zh: 我们现在看到的是哪座山峰？

sentences.en: And it's very hard to get a sense of where your bearings are when you're looking at those topographical maps.
sentences.zh: 看着这些地形图时，你很难弄清楚自己确切的方位。

sentences.en: And we were tired and confused.
And I just wanted to get in my sleeping bag and go to bed.
sentences.zh: 我只想钻进睡袋去睡觉。

sentences.en: So the group has to make a decision.
sentences.zh: 所以团队必须做一个决定。

sentences.en: You're not quite sure what to do.
sentences.zh: 你们不太确定该怎么做。

sentences.en: What do you end up doing?
And I basically say, look, you know, leaders are supposed to be decisive.
sentences.zh: 基本上我是这么说的：听着，领导就得有决断力。

sentences.en: I think we should move down the mountain.
And people pick up their bags and they start to follow me.
sentences.zh: 然后大家拿起背包，开始跟着我走。

sentences.en: At first, I was like, look, I'm excited to get back into my sleeping bag.
sentences.zh: 一开始，我还觉得：太好了，又能钻进睡袋了。

sentences.en: But then all of a sudden the terrain started to look different than what we were expecting.
sentences.zh: 但突然之间，地形开始变得跟我们预期得不一样了。

sentences.en: There didn't seem to be any water sources nearby.
sentences.zh: 附近好像没有任何水源。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, we started to feel a little bit like maybe we are going in the wrong direction.
sentences.zh: 所以，对，我们开始觉得是不是走错方向了。

sentences.en: But it was easier to keep moving than it was to admit that I was wrong.
sentences.zh: 但比起承认自己错了，继续往前走要容易得多。

sentences.en: You discover that you are not where you want to be.
sentences.zh: 你发现自己根本不在想去的地方。
谢天谢地，所有人都挺理解的。

sentences.en: And we're all relatively new to reading maps and orienting in the outdoors.
sentences.zh: 而且我们对看地图和户外辨向都挺生疏的。

sentences.en: But we look back at the map.
We try to orient ourselves again.
sentences.zh: 我们再次尝试辨别方向。

sentences.en: And we realized that the lake was above us the whole time.
sentences.zh: 然后我们发现，湖其实一直在我们的上方。

sentences.en: It was at a higher elevation, which is counterintuitive, right?
sentences.zh: 它在更高的海拔，这挺反直觉的，对吧？

sentences.en: The lake should be below us.
sentences.zh: 湖应该在我们下面才对。

sentences.en: So we packed up our stuff again after reexamining the map and trudged an extra couple of hours back to base camp.
sentences.zh: 于是重新审视地图后，我们又收拾好行囊，艰难地多走好几个小时回到了大本营。

sentences.en: But I know that I felt really bad about leading everyone in the wrong direction.
sentences.zh: 但我知道，把大家带错方向让我心里非常过意不去。

sentences.en: One thing I've noticed when I have lost my way, Bobby, is that if I miss my exit on the highway, for example,
sentences.zh: 博比，我注意到一件事，每当我迷路的时候，比如说在高速公路上错过了出口，

sentences.en: and I know that I have to go to the next exit and turn around and come back,
sentences.zh: 而且我知道我必须开到下一个出口调头再开回来，

sentences.en: that whole journey is just excruciating for me.
sentences.zh: 那段路程对我来说简直就是一种煎熬。

sentences.en: Because every second as I'm driving the wrong direction,
sentences.zh: 因为当我在朝错误方向开的每一秒里，

sentences.en: I know I'm going to have to come back and go the other direction.
sentences.zh: 我都清楚自己还得开回来，往另一个方向走。

sentences.en: And every step feels like it's painful.
sentences.zh: 而且每一步都觉得那么痛苦。

sentences.en: That must have been your experience as well.
sentences.zh: 你当时肯定也有这种体会。

sentences.en: Oh, my head was bowed as I was walking behind the group the whole time.
sentences.zh: 哦，一路上我都是低着头跟在大伙身后的。

sentences.en: So I'm wondering, as you were heading back, retracing your steps,
sentences.zh: 所以我在想，当你往回走、原路折返，

sentences.en: climbing back uphill up this mountainside,
did you have a chance to reflect on how you had gone wrong, Bobby?
sentences.zh: 博比，你有没有机会反思一下自己是怎么走错路的？

sentences.en: I think it started the reflection that took several months and several years after
sentences.zh: 我想，正是从那时开始的反思，持续了好几个月甚至好几年，

sentences.en: to really figure out what was going on in that moment.
sentences.zh: 才让我真正弄明白当时到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: Why was it that I was so eager to be over the decision and to be moving in the right direction?
sentences.zh: 为什么我当时那么急着做出决定、急着往正确的方向走？

sentences.en: And I think so much of it was discomfort with the uncertainty,
sentences.zh: 我想这很大程度上是因为无法忍受不确定性，

sentences.en: with hearing these dissenting opinions and wanting so much to be in my sleeping bag,
sentences.zh: 无法忍受听到这些不同的意见，而且太想钻进睡袋里，

sentences.en: In that moment, uncertainty was an obstacle.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，不确定性是个障碍。

sentences.en: I mean, I can put myself in your shoes.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我完全能设身处地为你着想。

sentences.en: Everyone around you is hungry or tired.
sentences.zh: 你周围每个人又饿又累。

sentences.en: You don't know which way you're going.
sentences.zh: 你不知道自己要走哪条路。

sentences.en: You're trying to get to the sleeping bag.
You don't know whether to go up or down.
sentences.zh: 你不知道该往上还是往下。

sentences.en: And just making a decision, any decision, feels better than being indecisive.
sentences.zh: 比起犹豫不决，做出决定——哪怕随便什么决定——都感觉要好得多。

sentences.en: When we come back, how to know when doubt and uncertainty can be our friends.
sentences.zh: 接下来我们将探讨：如何认识到怀疑和不确定性其实可以成为我们的朋友。
您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: As we go through life, all of us are going to face forks in the road.
sentences.zh: 在我们度过人生的过程中，所有人都会面临人生的十字路口。

sentences.en: Those can pop up in our personal lives and at work.
sentences.zh: 这些十字路口可能出现在我们的个人生活中，也可能出现在工作中。

sentences.en: They can rear up in emergency situations.
sentences.zh: 它们还可能在紧急情况下突然出现。

sentences.en: People might turn to you and say,
sentences.zh: 人们可能会转向你，说道：

sentences.en: And seeing their stress and panic,
sentences.zh: 看到他们的压力和恐慌，

sentences.en: and sensing your own stress and panic,
sentences.zh: 同时感应到你自己的压力和恐慌，

sentences.en: you might be tempted to find a way to quickly soothe the distress.
sentences.zh: 你可能会忍不住想找个方法来迅速平息这种焦虑。

sentences.en: A quick decision can feel reassuring.
sentences.zh: 快速做一个决定会让人感到安心。

sentences.en: It can make the fear subside.
But at the University of Virginia, Bobby Parmar says there are times when reassurance is not our friend.
sentences.zh: 但在弗吉尼亚大学，博比·帕马尔说，有时候这种安心并不是我们的朋友。

sentences.en: Bobby, your story of your mistake during the hike illustrates a common quirk of the mind,
sentences.zh: 博比，你徒步时犯错的故事说明了人类思维的一个常见怪癖，

sentences.en: which is that we hate to sit with uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 那就是我们讨厌与不确定性共处。

sentences.en: Talk about why this might be the case.
You know, when we're in school, we learn that being smart means getting the right answer.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们在学校里学到的是，聪明意味着得到正确的答案。

sentences.en: People like to be what I call right answer getters.
sentences.zh: 人们喜欢成为我所说的“标准答案搜寻者”。

sentences.en: Certainty makes us feel really great, right?
sentences.zh: 确定性能让我们感觉非常好，对吧？

sentences.en: It feels like we have agency and we have control over our lives.
sentences.zh: 这让我们觉得我们有自主权，并且能掌控自己的生活。

sentences.en: But there are also some serious downsides to certainty.

sentences.en: We generally think of doubt as a bad thing.

sentences.en: Bobby, we talked earlier about your trip to Wyoming and how you got yourself and the rest of your crew lost looking for a campsite.

sentences.en: This is a year later, and I'm with 12 of my MBA students, also now taking an outdoor leadership course in the wilderness in Patagonia.

sentences.en: Sitting with doubt feels like this very passive thing.
sentences.zh: “与怀疑共存”感觉像是一件非常被动的事情。

sentences.en: Everyone wants to sit with something that's uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 每个人都想与令人不适的事物共存。

sentences.en: What I've noticed when I examine people who are really good at making decisions under conditions of uncertainty
sentences.zh: 我观察那些在不确定条件下极其擅长做决策的人时发现，

sentences.en: is they're actively engaging the doubt.
sentences.zh: 他们是在积极地与怀疑打交道。

sentences.en: So they're naming what it is.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会说出这究竟是什么。

sentences.en: They're generating hypotheses about how to address it.
sentences.zh: 他们会提出关于如何应对它的假设。

sentences.en: They're looking for strengths and weaknesses in those hypotheses.
sentences.zh: 他们会寻找这些假设中的优势与劣势。

sentences.en: They're playing with different solutions, all of which are very active and engaged.
sentences.zh: 他们会权衡不同的解决方案，所有这些都非常积极且充满参与感。

sentences.en: One of the ways that you and others suggest that we can use doubt as this kind of hypothesis-building exercise
sentences.zh: 你和其他人建议我们可以将怀疑用作这种假设构建练习的方法之一，

sentences.en: is demonstrated in a study that looked at how military officers come up with decisions.
sentences.zh: 在一项关于军官如何做出决策的研究中得到了体现。

sentences.en: Tell me about the study and what it found.
sentences.zh: 请跟我讲讲这项研究及其发现。

sentences.en: This is such an interesting study.
sentences.zh: 这是一项非常有趣的研究。

sentences.en: So what they did is they compiled all of this complex information about a battlefield scenario.
sentences.zh: 他们的做法是汇编了关于战场情境的所有这些复杂信息。

sentences.en: You know, the weather, the direction and location of different armies and where they were situated,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，天气、不同军队的方向和位置及其所处地点，

sentences.en: And they gave all of this complex information to two types of participants.
sentences.zh: 他们将所有这些复杂信息提供给两类参与者。

sentences.en: And others were much more experienced.
And what they asked both of these groups to do is to say,
sentences.zh: 他们要求这两组人做的是，

sentences.en: why don't you read through all of this complex information?
sentences.zh: 你们为什么不把所有这些复杂信息通读一遍呢？

sentences.en: It's, you know, conflicting and uncertain.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这既矛盾又充满不确定性。

sentences.en: And write down some questions that you want to ask.
sentences.zh: 写下一些你想问的问题。

sentences.en: And then write down a strategy.
What do you think you should do in this situation?
sentences.zh: 你觉得在这种情况下你该怎么做？

sentences.en: And so after they captured all that information,
sentences.zh: 所以在他们收集了所有这些信息后，

sentences.en: they had an independent panel of judges look at the questions and the strategies of both of these groups.
sentences.zh: 他们找了一个独立的评审小组来查看这两组人的问题和策略。

sentences.en: One novice group, the captains, and the more experienced group, the generals.
sentences.zh: 一个是新手组，即船长组；另一个是更有经验的组，即将军组。

sentences.en: And they noticed some really interesting patterns.
sentences.zh: 他们注意到了一些非常有趣的规律。

sentences.en: The patterns that they noticed were novices were much more likely to treat their intuition as if it was their decision.
sentences.zh: 他们注意到的规律是，新手更有可能把他们的直觉当作他们的决定。

sentences.en: I think this is what we should do in the battle.
sentences.zh: 我想我们在战斗中应该这么做。

sentences.en: And here's some data that suggests that my strategy is the right strategy.
sentences.zh: 这里有一些数据表明我的策略是正确的策略。

sentences.en: With the exact same information, experts saw that data as much more complicated and nuanced.
sentences.zh: 面对完全相同的信息，专家们认为这些数据要复杂、微妙得多。

sentences.en: They decided to treat their intuition not as a decision, but as a hypothesis.
sentences.zh: 他们决定不把直觉当作一个决定，而是当作一个假设。

sentences.en: They were asking questions about key uncertainties.
sentences.zh: 他们围绕关键的不确定性提出问题。

sentences.en: They built strategies that were flexible and had mitigation strategies.
sentences.zh: 他们制定了灵活且包含缓解策略的策略。

sentences.en: So how could we fall back if something goes wrong?
sentences.zh: 那么如果出了问题，我们该如何退路呢？

sentences.en: The level of their thinking was just much more careful and nuanced than the novices, even with the same information.
sentences.zh: 与新手相比，即使面对相同的信息，他们的思考水平也要谨慎和微妙得多。

sentences.en: Is there evidence that this is true across different industries, Bobby?
sentences.zh: 博比，有没有证据表明这在不同行业中都是如此？

sentences.en: This is a finding that's been replicated in lots of different domains.
sentences.zh: 这是一个在许多不同领域都被复制过的发现。

sentences.en: You know, people who are experienced dealing with doubt are just much more sensitive to their surroundings.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有经验应对怀疑的人对周围环境要敏感得多。

sentences.en: So when we look at expert entrepreneurs, entrepreneurs who've started several businesses, when they talk about a business concept, they're just much more able to see,
sentences.zh: 所以当我们观察经验丰富的企业家，也就是那些创办过几家企业的企业家时，当他们谈论一个商业概念时，他们能够看得更清楚，

sentences.en: here are all the ways in which this business concept could impact different stakeholders.
sentences.zh: 这个商业概念可能会对不同的利益相关者产生影响的所有方式都在这里。

sentences.en: They're able to assess what are the unintended outcomes of this business concept.
sentences.zh: 他们能够评估这个商业概念的意外结果是什么。

sentences.en: And they can also think about, here, like the second or third order consequences of this business concept.
sentences.zh: 他们还可以思考，比如这个商业概念的第二或第三层级后果。

sentences.en: They're just much more careful thinkers.
sentences.zh: 他们的思考要谨慎得多。

sentences.en: When we look at nurses, when nurses are making an uncertain diagnosis, they collect twice as much data when compared to novice nurses about the exact same patient.
sentences.zh: 当我们观察护士时，当护士做出不确定的诊断时，与新手护士相比，他们针对完全相同的患者会收集两倍的数据。

sentences.en: Expert lawyers are much better at scanning the courtroom and adapting their arguments in real time based on what they're seeing in the jury.
sentences.zh: 经验丰富的律师更善于审视法庭，并根据他们在陪审团身上看到的情况实时调整他们的论点。

sentences.en: Expert writers spend a lot more time revising their drafts than novice writers.
sentences.zh: 经验丰富的作家花在修改草稿上的时间比新手作家多得多。

sentences.en: All of this suggests that people who are experienced when it comes to dealing with uncertainty and doubt are more sensitive to their surrounding and they're investing in learning.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切都表明，在应对不确定性和怀疑方面经验丰富的人对周围环境更敏感，并且他们正在投资于学习。

sentences.en: They're not investing in trying to get to a right answer quickly.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有把精力投入到试图快速找到正确答案上。

sentences.en: I mean, it's almost a paradox, Bobby.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这几乎是一个悖论，博比。

sentences.en: The people who are the most experienced are the most hesitant to quickly come to a conclusion.
sentences.zh: 最有经验的人反而是最迟疑于迅速得出结论的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's what I think is so interesting is many of us who are not at the top of our industry or running organizations who don't see ourselves as experts,
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得很有意思的是，我们当中许多人并不处于行业顶端，也没有管理组织，不觉得自己是专家，

sentences.en: look at experts and say, wow, they have the right answer and look how decisive they are.
sentences.zh: 看着专家会说，哇，他们有正确的答案，而且你看他们多么果断。

sentences.en: And then when you spend time with people who have significant experience and expertise, they're actually investing time in becoming what I call better answer makers,
sentences.zh: 然后，当你和那些具有丰富经验和专长的人在一起时，他们实际上是在花时间把自己变成我所说的更好答案的制造者，
而不是正确答案的获取者。

sentences.en: You say that some of this work points to another important strategy we can use to make better decisions, and it's called anomalizing.
sentences.zh: 你说其中一些工作指向了我们用来做出更好决策的另一个重要策略，这被称为“异常化”。

sentences.en: Anomalizing is basically looking for very early signals that something is departing from our expectations.
sentences.zh: 异常化基本上是寻找非常早期的信号，表明某事正在偏离我们的预期。

sentences.en: Going back all the way to when I was in Wyoming, looking at the ridgeline and saying, wait,
sentences.zh: 一直追溯到我在怀俄明州时，看着山脊线说，等等，

sentences.en: this is really different than what we would expect if the lake was nearby would be a form of anomalizing.
sentences.zh: 如果湖泊在附近，这与我们的预期截然不同，这就是一种异常化。

sentences.en: As a parent saying, oh, my kid isn't eating their lunch.
sentences.zh: 作为父母说，哦，我的孩子没有吃午饭。

sentences.en: I wonder if something is going wrong, is anomalizing.
sentences.zh: 我想知道是不是出了什么问题，这就是异常化。

sentences.en: So it's looking for early, weak signals that maybe our expectations aren't turning out the way that we anticipate.
sentences.zh: 所以它是在寻找早期的微弱信号，也许我们的预期并没有像我们预料的那样发展。

sentences.en: In other words, what you're trying to do is you're trying to say, how can I be wrong?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你想做的是试图问，我怎么才能证明自己是错的？

sentences.en: And a great way of practicing that in teams, in organizations, is something that's called a premortem.
sentences.zh: 在团队和组织中练习这一点的一个好方法叫做“事前验尸”。

sentences.en: So you take an idea, a strategy, we're going to launch a new product, or we're going to change this internal process, and before doing anything, we say, okay,
sentences.zh: 所以你拿出一个想法、一个策略，我们要推出一个新产品，或者我们要改变这个内部流程，在做任何事情之前，我们说，好吧，

sentences.en: let's imagine that we launched this product or we changed this process, and three weeks later, it failed.
sentences.zh: 让我们假设我们推出了这个产品或改变了这个流程，三周后，它失败了。

sentences.en: What is the most likely cause of death?
What is the most likely reason that we might fail?
sentences.zh: 我们可能失败的最可能原因是什么？

sentences.en: And by anticipating that most likely reason of failure, we can do something about it ahead of time.
sentences.zh: 通过预测那个最可能的失败原因，我们可以在事先采取行动。

sentences.en: In some ways, this builds on a very interesting idea, which is that many of us, in some ways, are able to look back at a decision and understand how that decision happened.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，这建立在一个非常有趣的观点之上，即我们中的许多人在某种程度上能够回顾一个决定并理解那个决定是如何发生的。

sentences.en: We have what's called hindsight bias.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有所谓的后见之明偏见。

sentences.en: So in some ways, this is taking advantage of our propensity to look back at an event that's already happened and try and use that hindsight bias in some ways prospectively to say,
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，这是在利用我们回顾已经发生的事件的倾向，并在某种程度上前瞻性地利用这种后见之明偏见，来说，

sentences.en: let's assume the bad thing has happened.
sentences.zh: 让我们假设糟糕的事情已经发生了。

sentences.en: Let's try and explain why this bad thing had happened.
sentences.zh: 让我们试着解释为什么这件糟糕的事情会发生。

sentences.en: And now you're using this fact-finding mission to basically say, how can we fix the problem before it happens?
sentences.zh: 现在你正在利用这个事实调查任务来基本上说明，我们如何在问题发生之前解决它？

sentences.en: How can we fix the problem?
sentences.zh: 我们如何解决这个问题？

sentences.en: Or if we run into the problem, how can we be adaptable and flexible to work our way around it?
sentences.zh: 或者如果我们遇到问题，我们如何保持适应性和灵活性来绕过它？

sentences.en: You give the very interesting example of Airbnb.
sentences.zh: 你举了一个非常有趣的例子，那就是Airbnb。

sentences.en: It's obviously a multibillion-dollar company with millions of properties around the world, clearly a huge success.
sentences.zh: 它显然是一家市值数十亿美元的公司，在全球拥有数百万处房产，显然取得了巨大的成功。

sentences.en: But in 2007, you say the company was on the verge of bankruptcy.
sentences.zh: 但你说在2007年，这家公司一度处于破产边缘。

sentences.en: You know, when you look at it on paper or on slide decks, the idea of having people rent out or lease their properties makes so much sense.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你在纸上或幻灯片上看到它时，让人们出租或租赁他们的房产这个想法非常有道理。

sentences.en: But in the actual implementation of the idea, the founders learned that they had some more work to do.
sentences.zh: 但在该想法的实际实施中，创始人了解到他们还有更多的工作要做。

sentences.en: So early on, they started to say, look, we built this beautiful system.
sentences.zh: 所以在早期，他们开始说，看，我们构建了这个漂亮的系统。
人们可以租赁他们的房产。

sentences.en: The back-end financial system works really well.
sentences.zh: 后端财务系统运行得非常好。

sentences.en: You can get credit card transactions to work.
sentences.zh: 你可以让信用卡交易顺畅运行。

sentences.en: But no one was actually renting properties.
sentences.zh: 但实际上没有人租房产。

sentences.en: And they couldn't figure out why.

sentences.zh: 所以他们变得非常好奇。

sentences.en: And they said, why don't we spend some time with some of our customers?
sentences.zh: 他们说，为什么我们不花点时间跟我们的一些客户在一起呢？

sentences.en: And they watched customers actually navigate the Airbnb website.
sentences.zh: 他们观察了客户实际浏览Airbnb网站的过程。

sentences.en: And one of the first things they learned is at the time when people were posting their properties in Manhattan, they were posting very grainy cell phone photos.
sentences.zh: 他们了解到的第一件事就是，当时人们在曼哈顿发布房产时，发布的是非常模糊的手机照片。

sentences.en: So you couldn't see the quality of the place that you were renting.
sentences.zh: 所以你根本看不到你所租地方的品质。

sentences.en: And people would say, well, why would I spend $250 or $300 a night for this place that looks really grainy?
sentences.zh: 人们会说，为什么我要为这个看起来非常模糊的地方每晚花250或300美元？

sentences.en: I can't quite tell what it is.
sentences.zh: 我根本分不清这是什么。

sentences.en: I could stay in a really nice hotel for the same price.
sentences.zh: 同样的价钱我可以住一家非常好的酒店。

sentences.en: And so that led them to this other hypothesis, which is, why don't we have someone take professional photos of some of these properties?
sentences.zh: 这让他们转向了另一个假设，那就是，为什么我们不找人给其中一些房产拍专业照片呢？

sentences.en: And they found very quickly that properties with professional photos rented very quickly.
sentences.zh: 他们很快发现，有专业照片的房产很快就被租出去了。

sentences.en: And what's important about this story is that many times when we're making decisions, we focus on the what.
sentences.zh: 这个故事的重要性在于，很多时候当我们做决定时，我们关注的是“什么”。

sentences.en: What's the business that we build in order to get people to be able to rent out property that they have?
sentences.zh: 为了让人们能够出租他们拥有的房产，我们建立的是什么业务？

sentences.en: We spend less attention to the how.
And when we focus on the what, it's really easy to have a big abstract vision that has lots of assumptions baked into it.
sentences.zh: 当我们关注“什么”时，很容易产生一个宏大抽象的愿景，其中包含大量的假设。

sentences.en: And there's lots of things that we don't know.
sentences.zh: 而且有很多事情是我们不知道的。

sentences.en: And we can convince ourselves that we're right.
sentences.zh: 我们可以说服自己我们是对的。

sentences.en: But when we focus on the how, we have to become much more specific.
sentences.zh: 但当我们关注“如何”时，我们必须变得更加具体。

sentences.en: And it focuses us to imagine with much more discipline and much more detail how we're going to get from point A to point B.
sentences.zh: 它迫使我们以更多的纪律和更多的细节去想象我们将如何从A点到达B点。

sentences.en: It also strikes me, Bobby, that so much of what you're talking about is so closely connected with the scientific method.
sentences.zh: 博比，我也觉得你所谈论的很多内容与科学方法紧密相连。

sentences.en: That if you think about why science itself has been effective, so radically effective over the last two centuries,
sentences.zh: 如果你想想为什么科学本身一直是有效的，在过去两个世纪里如此激进地有效，

sentences.en: so much of it has been about the embrace of doubt, the embrace of uncertainty, the testing of ideas, as opposed to just going with your gut.
sentences.zh: 很大程度上在于拥抱怀疑、拥抱不确定性、测试想法，而不是仅仅凭直觉行事。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's exactly right.
You know, observation, generation of hypothesis, testing those hypotheses and then leading to new observations is critical to learning.
sentences.zh: 你知道，观察、生成假设、测试这些假设，然后带来新的观察，这对学习至关重要。

sentences.en: What I think is really important to underscore when we think about the importance of the scientific method is that many times we think about learning as a predominantly cognitive endeavor.
sentences.zh: 当我们思考科学方法的重要性时，我认为真正需要强调的是，很多时候我们把学习主要看作是一种认知活动。

sentences.en: But when we embrace doubt, we have to understand that learning is just as much a social and emotional endeavor.
sentences.zh: 但当我们拥抱怀疑时，我们必须明白，学习同样是一种社会和情感活动。

sentences.en: And when we take doubt seriously, we take very seriously the way that people experience the world, both emotionally and socially, to preserve learning.
sentences.zh: 当我们认真对待怀疑时，我们非常认真地对待人们体验世界的方式，无论是在情感上还是在社会层面上，以维护学习。

sentences.en: So I'm getting a couple of things from this.
sentences.zh: 所以我从中得出了一些结论。

sentences.en: One is that I think when we sit with the problem and we sit with the doubts that we might have about a problem or sit with the uncertainties involved in the problem,
sentences.zh: 一个是，我认为当我们审视问题，审视我们对问题可能存在的怀疑，或者审视问题中涉及的不确定性时，

sentences.en: we start to see first how complex the problem is, that in fact, it's more complex than we might have allowed previously.
sentences.zh: 我们开始首先看到问题有多么复杂，事实上，它比我们之前允许自己认识到的要复杂得多。

sentences.en: But second, we also discover that there are actually more solutions than we initially thought about.
sentences.zh: 但其次，我们也发现，实际上解决方案比我们最初想象的要多。

sentences.en: When we cannot engage doubt, there are all kinds of phases in the decision-making process,
sentences.zh: 当我们无法面对怀疑时，在决策过程的各种阶段中，

sentences.en: from framing a problem to generating alternatives to testing those alternatives to implementation that we can inadvertently shortchange or rush through.
sentences.zh: 从构建问题到生成备选方案，再到测试这些备选方案直至实施，我们可能会无意中偷工减料或匆忙行事。

sentences.en: And when we're able to engage doubt, when we see it as a signal for learning, we don't rush through those stages.
sentences.zh: 而当我们能够面对怀疑，当我们将它视为学习的信号时，我们就不会匆忙通过这些阶段。

sentences.en: We can be much more effective in creating novel options, in implementing more effectively.
sentences.zh: 我们在创造新颖的选择、更有效地实施方面可以更加有效。

sentences.en: I think one of the important things to remember about doubt is that it's like the burn that we feel when we're working out at the gym on rep 8 or rep 9.
sentences.zh: 我认为关于怀疑，需要记住的重要事情之一是，它就像我们在健身房做第8次或第9次重复动作时感受到的肌肉酸痛。

sentences.en: If we were to give up in that moment, we'd be foregoing actually getting stronger.
sentences.zh: 如果我们在那个时刻放弃，我们就放弃了真正变得更强壮的机会。

sentences.en: And I think about doubt as that burn.
sentences.zh: 我把怀疑看作是那种酸痛。

sentences.en: It's a signal that I'm about to become much more capable.
sentences.zh: 这是一个信号，表明我即将变得更有能力。

sentences.en: I'm about to become stronger or wiser in that moment.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，我将变得更强壮或更明智。

sentences.en: And so when we experience doubt, remembering that it's a signal for growth rather than a signal that we're not smart is really important.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们经历怀疑时，记住它是成长的信号，而不是我们不够聪明的信号，这非常重要。

sentences.en: What do you make of political leaders who sound extremely confident today, Bobby?
sentences.zh: 博比，你如何看待今天听起来极其自信的政治领袖？

sentences.en: I'm wondering, when you watch the news and you see people make pronouncements with great confidence about things that will happen two years from now,
sentences.zh: 我在想，当你看着新闻，看到人们对两年后会发生的事情充满自信地做出断言时，

sentences.en: if a particular policy is implemented or not implemented, what goes through your head?
sentences.zh: 如果某项特定政策得以实施或未实施，你脑子里在想什么？

sentences.en: One of the things that I think in those moments is that, you know, it just feels like you're offering an addictive substance to your audience.
sentences.zh: 在那些时刻我脑子里闪过的一个想法是，你知道，这感觉就像你在向你的受众提供一种成瘾物质。

sentences.en: That in that moment, your audience is like, ah, there's some certainty.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，你的受众会觉得，啊，有了一些确定性。

sentences.en: And you're pulling people along in that moment.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，你在牵着人们的鼻子走。

sentences.en: No one can make those promises, but it feels so good to hear them in the moment.
sentences.zh: 没有人能做出那些承诺，但在那一刻听到它们感觉太好了。

sentences.en: So it's like offering some addictive substance that people have a hard time saying no to, even if they might know that it's not in their best long-term intereSt.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像提供某种让人很难拒绝的成瘾物质，即使他们可能知道这不符合他们的长期最佳利益。

sentences.en: In other words, even if they have been in some ways misled or disappointed in the past because your previous promises have failed to materialize,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，即使他们过去在某种程度上被误导或失望，因为你先前的承诺未能兑现，

sentences.en: the certainty that you're offering in some ways feels like a drug that basically says it limits the uncertainty I'm feeling and that makes me feel better.
sentences.zh: 你在某种程度上提供的确定性感觉就像是一剂药物，基本上它限制了我感受到的不确定性，这让我感觉好多了。

sentences.en: One of the things we have to really be careful of in the information age is this risk of the addiction to feeling right.
sentences.zh: 在信息时代，我们真正需要小心的危险之一就是对“感觉自己是对的”这种状态的成瘾。

sentences.en: All of our social media environments can be completely manufactured to help us feel good about our existing set of beliefs.
sentences.zh: 我们所有的社交媒体环境都可以被完全人为制造，来帮助我们对现有的信念感到良好。

sentences.en: And many of us come to associate that feeling of not knowing as very uncomfortable because we're so used to feeling right.
sentences.zh: 我们中的许多人开始将“不知道”的那种感觉与极不舒服联系起来，因为我们太习惯于感觉自己是对的了。

sentences.en: It can be an addictive thing.

sentences.en: Researcher Emily Falk returns to the show to answer listeners' questions about defensiveness.
sentences.zh: 研究员艾米莉·福尔克重返节目，回答听众关于戒备心理的问题。
您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: You know you shouldn't say anything.
It's really not such a big deal.
sentences.zh: 这其实真的算不上什么大事。

sentences.en: You tell yourself to keep the peace.
sentences.zh: 你告诉自己要息事宁人。

sentences.en: After all, does it really matter that your partner loads the dishwasher all wrong?
sentences.zh: 毕竟，你的伴侣洗碗的方式完全不对，这真的很重要吗？

sentences.en: But it does matter, whispers the little voice in your head.
sentences.zh: 但它确实很重要，你脑海中的那个小声音在低语。

sentences.en: Don't you remember the wine glass that broke last week?
sentences.zh: 你不记得上周碎了的那个酒杯了吗？

sentences.en: In all of our lives, the people around us do things that drive us up the wall.
sentences.zh: 在我们每个人的生活中，周围的人都会做一些让我们抓狂的事。

sentences.en: If it's not the way your partner loads the dishwasher, it's the way your dad backs into a parking space
sentences.zh: 如果不是你伴侣放碗碟的方式，那就是你爸爸倒车入库的方式

sentences.en: or your colleague's annoying tendency to interrupt you in a meeting.
sentences.zh: 又或者是你同事在开会时打断你的讨厌习惯。

sentences.en: Sometimes, we let these things slide.
sentences.zh: 有时候，我们会对这些事情视而不见。

sentences.en: At other times, we feel compelled to speak up, either for our own sake or for the other person's benefit.
sentences.zh: 而在其他时候，无论是为了我们自己还是为了对方的好处，我们会觉得不得不说出来。

sentences.en: But getting a good result from this sort of feedback is not easy.

sentences.en: Chances are, the other person will feel that we're picking on them or nagging.
sentences.zh: 很有可能，对方会觉得我们在挑刺或唠叨。

sentences.en: So, what can we do to make the process of giving and receiving feedback a little less fraught?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们能做些什么，让提出和接受反馈的过程不那么令人紧张呢？

sentences.en: That's where Emily Falk comes in.

sentences.en: Today, Emily returns to the show to address your comments
sentences.zh: 今天，艾米丽重返节目，来回应大家的评论

sentences.en: in our latest installment of our popular segment, Your Questions Answered.
sentences.zh: 在我们广受欢迎的栏目“你的问题解答”的最新一期中。

sentences.en: Emily Falk, welcome back to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 艾米丽·福尔克，欢迎回到《隐形大脑》。

sentences.en: Emily, you pointed out in our earlier conversation that one reason we respond defensively to feedback
sentences.zh: 艾米丽，你在之前的对话中指出，我们对反馈做出防御性反应的一个原因

sentences.en: is because our minds associate what is me with what is good.
sentences.zh: 是因为我们的头脑把“我是谁”和“什么是好的”联系在了一起。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that?
Well, in our brains, we have a system called the value system that helps us evaluate whether things are good or bad,
sentences.zh: 嗯，在我们的脑海中，我们有一个被称为价值系统的系统，它帮助我们评估事物是好是坏，

sentences.en: likely to be rewarding for us.
And we also have a self-relevance system that helps us decide whether things are me or not me.
sentences.zh: 我们还有一个自我相关系统，它帮助我们判断事物是“我”还是“非我”。

sentences.en: And interestingly, those two systems are really intertwined with one another.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，这两个系统确实是交织在一起的。

sentences.en: So the same kinds of brain patterns that differentiate between whether I think that a particular trait like messy or intelligent applies to me
sentences.zh: 因此，区分“我认为像‘凌乱’或‘聪明’这样的特定特质是否适用于我”的同类大脑模式

sentences.en: can also differentiate whether I'm looking at an image that I think is positive, like a birthday party,
sentences.zh: 也能区分我是在看一张我认为是积极的图片，比如生日派对，

sentences.en: or negative, like a pile of trash or a gory scene.
sentences.zh: 还是消极的，比如一堆垃圾或血腥的场景。

sentences.en: And in our day-to-day lives, this comes up in so many different places, starting with the physical things that we hold on to.
sentences.zh: 在我们的日常生活中，这种情况在许多不同的地方都会出现，首先是我们紧抓不放的实体物品。

sentences.en: So right now, I've been thinking a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，我一直在想很多。

sentences.en: I've been helping my mom navigate clearing out stuff in her house.
sentences.zh: 我一直在帮我妈妈清理她屋子里的东西。

sentences.en: And we have movers scheduled to come and take the rest of the stuff out of her house next week.
sentences.zh: 我们已经预约了搬家公司下周来把她屋里的其余东西搬走。

sentences.en: And in preparation for that, I have spent so much time recently going through a lot of my childhood things.
sentences.zh: 为了做准备，我最近花了很多时间整理我童年的许多物品。

sentences.en: So some of those things are really important and things that I'm going to hold dear,
sentences.zh: 其中有些东西真的很重要，是我会倍加珍惜的，

sentences.en: like the stool that my dad made for me, the little wooden stool that has an E on it when I was a kid, that 100% I'm keeping.
sentences.zh: 比如我爸爸为我做的凳子，那个我小时候用过的、上面刻有字母E的小木凳，我百分之百会留着。

sentences.en: But then there's also stuff that would just be clutter,
sentences.zh: 但也有一些东西纯粹就是杂物，

sentences.en: like all of the textbooks and notebooks that have hundreds of pages of notes that I took in high school and college.
sentences.zh: 比如我在高中和大学里记了数百页笔记的所有的教科书和笔记本。

sentences.en: Like the things that I learned about, you know, revolutions in Central America in high school,
sentences.zh: 就像我学过的一些东西，你知道的，高中时关于中美洲革命的那些，

sentences.en: there are books that do a much better job of describing those situations than my, you know, partial understanding as a 16-year-old.
sentences.zh: 有些书在描述这些情况时比我（你知道的，作为一个16岁少年的片面理解）要做得好得多。

sentences.en: And yet, going through those notebooks and seeing my handwriting and thinking about who I was at the time,
sentences.zh: 然而，翻看这些笔记本，看到自己的笔迹，想起当时的自己，

sentences.en: it feels so hard to let go of those things and throw them out.
sentences.zh: 让人感觉要放下这些东西并把它们扔掉是如此艰难。

sentences.en: And I think that comes from this idea that things that I think of as me are also then kind of inherently valuable
sentences.zh: 我想这源于这样一种观念：我认为是“我”的东西，然后也会在某种程度上具有内在的价值，

sentences.en: in a different way than, you know, looking at somebody else's notebook.
sentences.zh: 这与你知道的，去看别人的笔记本有着不同的感觉。

sentences.en: I can see that that's probably not something that I need to keep.
sentences.zh: 我能看出那可能不是我需要保留的东西。

sentences.en: And so that intertwining of self and value is sometimes really beneficial
sentences.zh: 因此，“自我”与“价值”的这种交织有时真的很有益，

sentences.en: because it helps us maintain a positive sense of self.
sentences.zh: 因为它有助于我们维持积极的自我感。

sentences.en: But it can also get us in trouble because we hold really tightly to the things that we've done in the past
sentences.zh: 但它也可能会给我们带来麻烦，因为我们紧抓着过去做过的事情不放，

sentences.en: or to things that we think of as being part of us.
sentences.zh: 或者紧抓着我们认为是自己一部分的东西不放。

sentences.en: So in other words, when your partner tells you that you're loading the dishwasher wrong,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，当你的伴侣告诉你你洗碗的方式不对时，

sentences.en: you're not just hearing that there might be a different way to load the dishwasher.
sentences.zh: 你听到的不仅仅是可能还有另一种装洗碗机的方法。

sentences.en: You're also hearing in some ways an attack on this sense of self.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，你听到的也是对这种自我感的攻击。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that the ways that we tend to conflate self and value can get us in trouble in exactly that way,
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为我们倾向于将自我和价值混为一谈的方式，正会在这一点上给我们带来麻烦，

sentences.en: that somebody is giving us advice or coaching or input that might otherwise be beneficial for us.
sentences.zh: 也就是当别人给我们提出建议、指导或意见时，这些意见本来对我们是有益的。

sentences.en: And instead of hearing the potentially valuable kernel of truth,
sentences.zh: 但我们听到的不是那些可能很有价值的真相核心，

sentences.en: we hear something that is suggesting all kinds of things about who we are
sentences.zh: 而是听到了一些暗示，它们指向我们是谁的方方面面，

sentences.en: and maybe what we're capable of or evaluating something bigger than might be at stake there.
sentences.zh: 也许还有我们的能力，或者是在评估比当前赌注更大的东西。

sentences.en: One of the things we talk about with some regularity on Hidden Brain
sentences.zh: 我们在《隐形大脑》中经常谈论的事情之一

sentences.en: is the fact that we assess ourselves by our intentions,
sentences.zh: 就是这样一个事实：我们通过自己的意图来评估自己，

sentences.en: but other people don't necessarily know what we intended to do.
sentences.zh: 但其他人并不一定知道我们打算做什么。

sentences.en: They can only see our actions.
sentences.zh: 他们只能看到我们的行动。

sentences.en: Do you think the fact that we have insight into our own thoughts and intentions
sentences.zh: 你认为，正是因为我们对自己的想法和意图有深刻的洞察，

sentences.en: is why we feel defensive sometimes when someone critiques our actions?
sentences.zh: 才导致我们在别人批评我们的行为时有时会感到防备吗？

sentences.en: That's a really interesting way of framing it.
sentences.zh: 这真的是一种很有趣的构建方式。

sentences.en: I think that this idea that we can understand why we did something is such a valuable insight
sentences.zh: 我认为这种“我们可以理解自己为什么做某事”的想法是一个非常有价值的见解，

sentences.en: for when we're the person giving the critique.
sentences.zh: 当我们是提出批评的那个人时尤其如此。

sentences.en: So when we think about how we're going to frame the request for our partner to load the dishwasher differently,
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们思考如何措辞来要求伴侣以不同方式装洗碗机时，

sentences.en: there might be all kinds of things that are on their minds that we don't have access to.
sentences.zh: 他们的脑海里可能会充斥着各种我们无法触及的事情。

sentences.en: And so what you're proposing is that on the other side of it,
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，换个角度来看，

sentences.en: we also think it's really obvious why we did what we did.
sentences.zh: 我们也觉得我们为什么这样做是显而易见的。

sentences.en: There are so many reasons that are salient in terms of what happened already in our day
sentences.zh: 由于我们当天已经发生的事情或过去的经历，有太多的理由显而易见。

sentences.en: or other past experiences we've had.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极其容易产生各种误解的领域。

sentences.en: That's a space that's rife for miscommunication of all kinds.

sentences.zh: 我在想一个教练，他基本上是在指导一个运动员，

sentences.en: I'm thinking about a coach who's basically advising an athlete
sentences.zh: 并要求运动员做一些能够提高运动员表现的事情。

sentences.en: and is asking the athlete to do something that would improve the athlete's performance.
sentences.zh: 而运动员心里想的是，但你不知道我有多么精疲力竭，我有多累，

sentences.en: And the athlete is thinking, but you don't know how exhausted I am, how tired I am,
sentences.zh: 我有多少不同的事情要在脑子里应付。

sentences.en: how many different things I'm juggling in my head.
sentences.zh: 你只是要求我多做这一件额外的事，

sentences.en: You're just asking me to do this one additional thing,
sentences.zh: 而你根本没有关注所有的背景。

sentences.en: and you're not paying attention to all the context.
sentences.zh: 这会让我很难听从你的建议。

sentences.en: That's going to make it difficult for me to follow your advice.
sentences.zh: 哦，我很高兴你举了教练的例子，

sentences.en: Oh, I love that you bring up the coach example,
sentences.zh: 因为我认为教练的例子是一个双方都同意了参与条款的情境。

sentences.en: because I think the coach example is a situation where we've both agreed on the terms of engagement.

sentences.zh: 我们已经同意，如果你是教练而我是运动员，

sentences.en: We've agreed that if you're the coach and I'm the athlete,
sentences.zh: 我想我一定是报名来听取你的建议的。

sentences.en: presumably I've signed up to get your advice.
sentences.zh: 我们也同意，你正在试图做一些符合我利益的事情，

sentences.en: And we've also agreed that you are trying to do something that's in my interest,
sentences.zh: 那就是让我在这项运动或活动中变得更好。

sentences.en: which is make me better at whatever the sport or activity is.
sentences.zh: 因此，举个例子，如果我付钱请你当我的游泳教练，而你给了我一些建议，

sentences.en: So if I'm paying you to be my swim coach, for example, and you give me some advice,
sentences.zh: 这实际上真的降低了我说出这样一番话的几率：

sentences.en: it actually really reduces the chance that I'm going to say,
sentences.zh: “嗯，你知道的，尚卡尔凭什么告诉我该那样做？”

sentences.en: well, you know, why is Shankar telling me to do it that way?
sentences.zh: 因为参与条款比洗碗机的情况要清晰得多，

sentences.en: Because the terms of engagement are much clearer than the dishwasher situation,
sentences.zh: 在洗碗机的情况中，有太多其他变量在起作用，你知道的，我可不是你洗碗机方面的教练。

sentences.en: where there are so many other variables at play where, you know, I'm not your dishwasher coach.
sentences.zh: 所以我们并没有真正就我向你提供有关这类家务活的意见达成一致。

sentences.en: And so we haven't actually agreed that I give you input about those kinds of household chores.

sentences.zh: 事实上，在某些情况下，我们双方都认为自己是教练，而对方是受训者。

sentences.en: And in fact, in some situations, we both think that we are the coach and the other person is our trainee.

sentences.zh: 所以，我们听取了几位听众打进的电话，他们分享了自己在应对手足无措的朋友或家人时遇到的困难，

sentences.en: So we heard from several people who called in to share the difficulties they've had
sentences.zh: 这些人对反馈有着防御心理。

sentences.en: in dealing with friends or family members who get defensive about feedback.
sentences.zh: 这是我们收到的听众凯蒂（Katie）的一条留言。

sentences.en: Here's a message we received from listener Katie.
sentences.zh: 在面对一个高度防备甚至具有攻击性的挚爱之人时，一个人如何能保持冷静和沉着，

sentences.en: How can someone stay calm and grounded when dealing with a loved one who becomes highly defensive or even aggressive,
sentences.zh: 特别是当这种反应感觉不成比例或针对个人时？

sentences.en: especially when the reaction feels disproportionate or personal?
sentences.zh: 基本上，你如何在不吸收或陷入负能量的情况下尊重他们的感受？

sentences.en: Basically, how do you honor their feelings without absorbing or engaging in the negativity?
sentences.zh: 艾米丽，我真的很喜欢凯蒂提出这个困境的方式。

sentences.en: I really like the way that Katie presents this dilemma, Emily.
sentences.zh: 当我们进行艰难的对话时，承认对方的感受是很重要的。

sentences.en: When we're having a tough conversation, it can be important to acknowledge how the other person is feeling.
sentences.zh: 但是，当我们觉得某人的反应与眼前的局势不成比例时，

sentences.en: But when we feel that someone's response is disproportionate to the situation at hand,
sentences.zh: 要承认他们全部的感受，而不是说“听我说”，可能会非常困难。

sentences.en: it can be really difficult to acknowledge all of what they are feeling instead of saying,

sentences.zh: 首先，作为一点背景知识，
这里有一个了不起的神经科学研究，它关于我们带入互动中的假设，

sentences.en: First of all, just as a little bit of background,
